issues.failure_explanation: The proof bounds dim M by dim L via the declared well-defined injective operator x -> Cx from M = ker(BC)^perp ∩ ker_c(ABC) to L = ker(B)^perp ∩ ker_c(AB). Although Cx always lies in ker_c(AB), it need not lie in ker(B)^perp: for z in ker(B), <Cx,z> = <x,C*z>, and C*z need not belong to ker(BC). Counterexample (H = F, all spaces two-dimensional): A = diag(0,1), B = diag(1,0), C = [[1,1],[0,1]]. Then ker(BC) = span{(1,-1)}, ker_c(ABC) = F^2, so M = span{(1,1)} and L = span{e_1}, but C(1,1) = (2,1) is not in L. Hence the key estimate dim M = dim im(C) <= dim L is unjustified as written. The Frobenius inequality itself is true (it holds for any composition of linear maps), but this argument does not establish it.

failure_location.quote: Consider $\Matrix{x} \mapsto \Matrix{Cx}$ as an injective linear operator $\Linop{C} : \mathbb{M} \to \mathbb{L}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the orthogonal complements by quotient null spaces: the induced map ker_c(ABC)/ker(BC) -> ker_c(AB)/ker(B), [x] -> [Cx], is well defined (ker(BC) maps into ker(B)) and injective, which yields dim M <= dim L and hence the claimed inequality.
issues.overall_effect: Only the proof of part 2 of lemma:rank_nullity is defective; the statement is correct, so after a local proof repair the derived Sylvester inequality (part 3 of the same lemma), lemma:rank_properties, and all downstream results stand unchanged.
issues.title: Frobenius-inequality proof: the map x -> Cx does not land in the claimed space L
issues.why_classification: The statement is true and the repair is a short, standard modification of one proof step; every downstream claim, guarantee, and scope survives verbatim.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: $\bm{2.}$ Note that $\Matrix{B}^\pinv \Matrix{B} = \Matrix{I}_{m}$ and $\Matrix{C} \Matrix{C}^\pinv = \Matrix{I}_{n}$, then substitute $\Matrix{C}^\pinv \Batrix{A}^\pinv \Matrix{B}^\pinv$ into Theorem~\ref{theorem:pinv_bochner}.

issues.failure_explanation: The candidate X = C^dagger A^dagger B^dagger satisfies Penrose conditions 1, 2, and 4, but not condition 3: (BAC)X = B(AA^dagger)B^dagger need not be self-adjoint, because the Bochner orthogonal projection AA^dagger onto im_c(A) acts entrywise through H-inner products and does not commute with the entrywise scalar action of usual matrices on H^m; the asserted substitution into the four Penrose conditions therefore does not go through. Counterexample: let h_1, h_2 in H be orthonormal, m = k = 2, n = l = 1, A = (h_1,h_2)^T (full column rank), B = [[1,1],[0,1]] (invertible), C = [1]. Then (BA)^dagger y = (<y_1,h_1+h_2> + <y_2,h_2>)/3 whereas A^dagger B^dagger y = (<y_1,h_1> - <y_2,h_1> + <y_2,h_2>)/2; at y = (0,h_1) the two values are 0 and -1/2. So the identity fails even with A of full column rank and B invertible. (For usual matrices the two-sided law additionally needs the middle factor to have full column rank; in the Bochner case the left-factor part fails regardless.)

failure_location.quote: If $\Matrix{B} \in \F^{k \times m}$ has full column rank and $\Matrix{C} \in \F^{n \times l}$ has full row rank, $(\Matrix{B} \Batrix{A} \Matrix{C})^\pinv = \Matrix{C}^\pinv \Batrix{A}^\pinv \Matrix{B}^\pinv$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Weaken the statement to a valid product rule: e.g., (AC)^dagger = C^dagger A^dagger for Bochner A of full column rank and usual C of full row rank (which also covers the implicit use in lemma:cur_column), and/or require B to have orthonormal columns for a left-factor identity; the general two-sided identity must be dropped.
issues.overall_effect: Part 2 of lem:added-8 is invalid as stated. No other labelled result cites it; the pseudoinverse manipulations in the proof of lemma:cur_column use only the valid special case (ĜX)^dagger = X^dagger Ĝ^dagger with Ĝ of full column rank, so the damage is confined to this one statement.
issues.title: Reverse-order pseudoinverse law (BAC)^dagger = C^dagger A^dagger B^dagger is false for Bochner matrices
issues.why_classification: The claimed identity is false and must be abandoned in its stated generality, which is more than a typo or a routine added condition; however, a recognizably comparable restricted rule survives and no labelled result depends on it, so the loss is contained.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The sets $\mathbb{M}_{\leq \kappa}$ and $\mathbb{M}_{\preccurlyeq (\rho,\kappa)} = \set{\Batrix{B} \in \Hilb^{m \times n}}{\Rank{T}{\Batrix{B}} \preccurlyeq (\rho,\kappa)}$ are closed.

issues.failure_explanation: In the Hilbert space H^{m×n} with a possibly infinite-dimensional H, closedness of the non-convex set M_{≼(ρ,κ)} does not by itself imply that the distance to it is attained, so the existence of C_* is unsupported as written. (Existence is in fact true here — e.g., by parametrizing admissible approximants as Q E with Q in the compact Stiefel manifold of usual ρ-frames and rank_c(E) <= κ, and applying Mirsky's theorem to the inner minimization — and, more importantly, the theorem's inequality never needs a minimizer: M_{≼(ρ,κ)} ⊆ M_{≤κ} already gives ||Σ_κ^c|| <= inf_{C in M_≼(ρ,κ)} ||A − C||, and similarly for the transpose.)

failure_location.quote: Since $\mathbb{M}_{\preccurlyeq (\rho,\kappa)}$ is closed, there is a minimizer $\Batrix{C}_\ast \in \mathbb{M}_{\preccurlyeq (\rho,\kappa)}$ of $\Norm{\Batrix{A} - \Batrix{C}}{\ell_2(\Hilb)}$ over $\mathbb{M}_{\preccurlyeq (\rho,\kappa)}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Remove the minimizer detour and bound ||Σ_κ^c|| and ||Λ_ρ^c|| directly by inf_{C in M_{≼(ρ,κ)}} ||A − C|| using the inclusions M_{≼(ρ,κ)} ⊆ M_{≤κ} and its transposed analogue.
issues.overall_effect: Only the existence sentence inside the proof is unsupported; the stated HOSVD quasi-optimality bound, and its later use in the numerics and discussion sections, are preserved by a direct infimum argument.
issues.title: HOSVD quasi-optimality proof infers existence of a best Tucker-rank approximant from closedness alone
issues.why_classification: A trivial bypass restores the full statement with no change to hypotheses, conclusions, or dependents; the unsupported side-claim is true and simply removable.

issues.failure_explanation: The text claims that u(x;α,β) = (2/π) Σ_k u_k(α,β) sin(kx) with the displayed coefficients is the solution of −u'' − α²u = cos(βx) on (0,π) with u(0)=u(π)=0. The sine coefficients of cos(βx) on (0,π) are k[1−(−1)^k cos(βπ)]/(k²−β²), and the operator −d²/dx² − α² multiplies the k-th sine mode by k² − α², so the true coefficients are k[1−(−1)^k cos(βπ)]/[(k²−α²)(k²−β²)]. The printed formula, with (k²+α²)(k²+β²), solves no sign variant of the stated equation with right-hand side cos(βx): both denominator signs are inconsistent. Moreover, the stated −α² problem is resonant at integer α in {1,2} ⊂ [0,α_max] = [0,2] (at α = 1 a solution exists only when cos(βπ) = −1), so as stated it does not even define the smooth solution map that the section sets out to approximate.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Make the two displays consistent in the non-degenerate regime: state the equation as −u'' + α²u = cos(βx) and the coefficients as u_k = k[1−(−1)^k cos(βπ)]/[(k²+α²)(k²−β²)] (with the removable limiting value at integer β), and regenerate the illustrative data accordingly.
